title: Fluency: a range that catches the truth

families.skill: a confidence interval from a standard error
families.prompt: A backtest gives $\bar x = {xb}\%$ a day, with $\mathrm{{SE}} = {se}\%$. What is the {lev}% confidence interval for $\mu$? Give both ends in %, to 3 decimal places.

wrong.line: You went one standard error each way. A {lev}% interval goes ${z}$ standard errors each way.
You used 1.96, the 95% multiplier. For {lev}% the multiplier is ${z}$.

solution: The {lev}% multiplier is ${z}$, so the half-width is ${z} \times {se} = {hw}\%$.
The interval runs from ${xb} - {hw} = {lo}$ to ${xb} + {hw} = {hi}$, in %.

families.skill: the half-width from a sample sd
families.prompt: A {n}-day backtest has sample sd $s = {s}\%$. What is the half-width of the {lev}% interval for its mean daily return, in %, to 3 decimal places?

wrong.line: You used $s$ in place of the standard error. Divide $s$ by $\sqrt{{{n}}} = {rt}$ first.
You divided $s$ by $n = {n}$. The standard error is $s/\sqrt n$, with $\sqrt{{{n}}} = {rt}$.

solution: The {lev}% half-width is ${z} \times {se} = {key}$, or ${key:dp3}\%$ to 3 decimal places.
